extracted.intended_audience: romance writers (members and prospective members), especially RWA/NYC chapter members and unpublished manuscript contest entrants
extracted.subtask_description: A workshop-focused subtask: creating an irresistible short blurb/hook for a romance novel by emphasizing the most compelling story elements and adapting them by subgenre. Also relevant to unpublished authors preparing submissions for chapter contests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight character, conflict, chemistry, and stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Along the way, you’ll discover how to highlight character, conflict, chemistry, and stakes—and how those elements shift across romance subgenres from romcom to romantic suspense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This workshop teaches you to foreground the protagonist(s), the central conflict, the emotional/sexual chemistry between leads, and what’s at risk (stakes) in a blurb so readers will be compelled to read/buy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt blurb elements to subgenre
rubrics_metrics.description: How those elements shift across romance subgenres from romcom to romantic suspense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The relative emphasis and tone for character, conflict, chemistry, and stakes should change depending on subgenre (e.g., romcom emphasizes humor and meet-cute/chemistry, romantic suspense emphasizes danger/stakes). Tailor wording, stakes, and implied tone to fit subgenre expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a simple, repeatable structure for blurbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Using guided prompts, trope challenges, and a simple, repeatable structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn a practical framework you can apply to your own books right away — a concise, repeatable blurb structure that helps consistently turn story elements into a compelling hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an irresistible hook that makes readers click 'buy now'
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncovering the key ingredients that make romance readers click “buy now.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus the blurb on the immediate, most compelling question or promise (the hook). The goal is to convert curiosity into a purchase decision by clearly communicating stakes, conflict, and emotional payoff in minimal words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use collaborative, gamified exercises to generate blurbs
rubrics_metrics.description: In this fast-paced, interactive workshop, we’ll turn blurb writing into a game—Working in teams, you’ll build a blurb from the ground up using guided prompts, trope challenges, and a simple, repeatable structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employing team-based, prompt-driven, and trope-challenging activities can help surface strong, creative hook ideas quickly and reveal alternative angles you might not find working alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest eligibility: unpublished manuscript requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: We run an annual contest for unpublished manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter’s Big Apple Contest is explicitly for unpublished manuscripts; entrants should verify they meet the 'unpublished' eligibility before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership requirement to join RWA/NYC (procedural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: You must be a member of Romance Writers of America to join RWA/NYC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership dues $35.00. This is a procedural requirement for chapter membership and access to members-only resources/events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational standard: promote excellence and advance professional interests
rubrics_metrics.description: We strive to promote excellence in romantic fiction and advance the professional interests of career-focused romance writers through networking, advocacy, dissemination of information, professional education, and publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter evaluates its activities (events, panels, contests) by how well they support excellence in craft, professional development, networking, and dissemination of industry knowledge to members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive publishing approach (no single 'right' publishing path)
rubrics_metrics.description: RWA/NYC believes authors should embrace whatever publishing avenue works best for them. Therefore, we have authors who are traditionally published, self-published and hybrid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality and professional success are measured across traditional, self-, and hybrid publishing models; members are encouraged to pursue the best route for their goals rather than adhere to a single publishing standard.
